scores.Biological Plausibility_reason: The HNRNPLL–PTPRC alternative-splicing mechanism is established and biologically coherent for activation-associated CD45 isoform switching in T cells. Its extrapolation as the principal explanation across mixed cord-blood immune populations, particularly naive B and non-lymphoid cells, is less well supported.
scores.Grounded Mechanistic Synthesis_reason: The response explicitly connects TCR activation, HNRNPLL induction, PTPRC exon exclusion, CD45RA loss, and the reciprocal CD45RO-associated memory state. It does not adequately connect this T-cell-centered mechanism to variation among B cells and other immune lineages in the mixed cord-blood sample. No synthesis ceiling was applied because the principal focus-to-target mechanism is explicit, multistep, and biologically defensible.
